title: sprint-05: operations (daily run, drift gate with approval, faults, scored questions)
goal: Run the forecast every day without re-choosing methods, notice when the methods have stopped working and stop for a person before retraining, end every failure in a stated state that a rerun recovers from, and score the assistant against the database.
pattern: LangGraph run graph (fetch, check, gate, forecast, finish) with a Postgres checkpoint per step, an interrupt at the gate and a run log
findings: Mutation check: 49/49 mutations killed (the sprint-05 mutants).

Real daily run torrance-2026-11-15: ended ok (reselect). The drift check flagged 1 of 14 lead/variable pairs (tmin 1 day ahead: recent miss 1.866 C against 0.697 C when the method was chosen), so the run stopped at the gate before any retraining. Decision recorded: approved.
Fault injection: 13 of 13 checks passed (API outage, late data, database restart mid-run, database down, planted drift).
Question set against the live model: 42/42 attempts passed; 14/14 cases passed every attempt.

01_eval.csv.title: Question set, live model, each case asked three times
01_eval.csv.note: passed = attempts that met every check of the case. Expected values are read from the database when the evaluation runs. refused_by_number_check counts attempts whose answer was withheld.

02_drift_check.csv.title: Drift check of the real daily run (torrance-2026-11-15)
02_drift_check.csv.note: recent_mae_c = this project's average miss over the last 30 scored days; baseline_mae_c = its miss on the held-out year when the method was chosen. n_live = days scored on a forecast issued live (the rest are replays). drifted = at least 14 days, over 1.5 times the baseline and over 0.5 C worse.

03_run_log.csv.title: Run log (app_run_log) for Torrance
03_run_log.csv.note: One row per day. waiting_approval = stopped at the gate.

04_drift_evidence_1_tmin_lead1.csv.title: Evidence behind the drift flag: 1 tmin lead1
04_drift_evidence_1_tmin_lead1.csv.note: Average miss and bias per month from the replayed forecasts. bias below 0 = forecast too cold.

limits: Drift is measured almost entirely on replayed forecasts so far: the live log started on 2026-11-14. The replay's models were fitted a year before, so part of what the check sees is that age, which a daily refit already removes.

For that reason the flag did not clear after the approved re-selection on 2026-11-15: the same methods were chosen again, the refitted model now adds about 1.9 C to the published low for tomorrow, and the check still reads 1.93 C against 0.70 C because it scores the year-old replay, not the model that runs. The run does not ask again for 7 days. Scoring only live forecasts needs at least 14 live days.
The drift rule (30 days, 1.5 times, 0.5 C) is a judgement, not tuned on data.

The mutation run for this sprint hung once (a test process idle for 4.5 hours, no time limit in the script). It was stopped, a time limit added, and the rest run as three workers, each on its own copy of the tree and its own test database.
The question set is 14 cases written by the author of the assistant; three attempts each show run-to-run variation, not a confidence interval.
The 'declines' rule of the grader is a phrase match. It shows the answer said no, not that everything else in it is right.
Fault injection runs on a small synthetic city in the test database with a stand-in for the weather APIs; the database restart and stop are real.
The 79 + 52 mutants of sprints 01-04 were not rerun this sprint.
No scheduler is installed: `make daily` is run by hand or by a scheduled task the user sets up.
